Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 8737 of 2023
Applicant :- Ajay Shukla Alias Rohit Shukla
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Deptt. Of Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Dinesh Kr. Chaudhary
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the sister of the informant was married with the applicant 28.05.2021 and sufficient dowry was also given.
Subsequently, on 07.07.2022 she was beaten and burnt to death.
The post mortem report on record indicates the cause of death as ante mortem burn injuries.
3. In the light of the said, the submission of the counsel for the applicant is that in the inquest report, the applicant was present.
He also argues that even at the post mortem, the applicant was Ajay Shukla Alias Rohit Shukla vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Deptt. Of Home ...

It is further argued that from the report of the I.O. of the site, where the incident had occurred, it is specifically recorded that after catching fire, the wall was broken and the fire was doused.
In the light of the said, it is argued that no role can be attributed to the applicant of having caused the burn injuries.

It is further argued that the entire matrimonial family was named in the FIR and subsequently, charge sheet was filed against only four accused and three of the co-accused including father, mother and brother of the applicant have been enlarged on bail.
It is also argued that the applicant is in custody since 22.07.2022 having no criminal history, as such, he may be enlarged on bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

5. Considering the fact that three co-accused have already been enlarged on bail coupled with the fact that the applicant was present during inquest as well as during post mortem and there is nothing on record to suggest that soon before the death, the deceased was subjected to any mental or physical torture in relation to the demand of dowry and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Ajay Shukla Alias Rohit Shukla be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 52 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Maharajganj Tarai,
District Balrampur, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
